American Time Use Survey (ATUS)About · Using this site

About this site

This site describes the American Time Use Survey (ATUS), published by U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). It is generated from the repository pdt-atus, which holds metadata built from the publisher's documentation: each variable's label, question text, codes and missing codes, and availability, with corrections and links between releases. Each fact says where it came from.

What it isn't

  • It isn't the publisher's site, and the publisher hasn't reviewed it. The publisher's own page for the dataset is https://www.bls.gov/tus/. Where this site and the publisher's documentation differ, the publisher's documentation is the source; the differences this repository knows of are listed as corrections.
  • It doesn't hold the data. The data come from the publisher, or from this repository's data release when the terms allow; see Getting the data.
  • It makes no analysis decisions: which answers count as agreement, which weights or cases to use, or how to recode. Those belong to the projects that use the data.

Terms of use

Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey, 2003-2025 multi-year files. BLS data are in the public domain; BLS asks to be cited as the source.
Publisher's terms
https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm
What they say
What BLS says (read 2026-11-20): its copyright page, https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm, says "everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations" and "You are free to use our public domain material without specific permission, although we do ask that you cite the Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source." No ATUS page states other terms of use for the microdata. Separately, BLS's terms (https://www.bls.gov/bls/blsterms.htm) reserve "the right to block robots that do not contain information that can be used to contact the owner": that limits how files are fetched, not how they are used, and is why every source is downloaded by hand.

PublicDataToolkit

The library and the standard that build this site: https://github.com/AllenDowney/PublicDataToolkit. This site was generated by version 0.2.0.

Reporting an error

  • In the publisher's documentation (a wrong label, a missing code, question text that belongs to another item): open an issue at the issue tracker of the repository pdt-atus, with where you found it. This repository records such errors as corrections, with the evidence, and keeps the publisher's original; it also says whether the error was reported to the publisher.
  • In this repository's records (a wrong link, a code classified wrongly, a variable left out): open an issue at the issue tracker of the repository pdt-atus.
  • To the publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
